title: Knaster-Tarski Proof of Schroeder-Bernstein
description: The Schroeder-Bernstein theorem proved via the Knaster-Tarski fixed point theorem: the monotone operator T(S) = (range g)ᶜ ∪ g''(f''S) on Set α has a least fixed point S* that partitions α into the bijection h(a) = f(a) for a ∈ S*, h(a) = g⁻¹(a) otherwise.

overview.historicalContext:
The Knaster-Tarski fixed point theorem (1928/1955) states that every monotone endomorphism of a complete lattice has a least fixed point. Tarski observed that the Schroeder-Bernstein theorem is a direct consequence: given injections f : α → β and g : β → α, the operator T(S) = α \ g(β \ f(S)) on the power set lattice P(α) is monotone, and its fixed point yields the bijection.

This connection was noted by Knaster and Tarski but is less well-known than the orbit decomposition proof. It reveals CBS as an instance of a fundamental lattice-theoretic principle, connecting cardinal arithmetic to order theory.

The proof is conceptually the simplest: no orbit classification, no induction, just one application of the fixed point theorem.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (OQ-02)**: Can we formalize the Knaster-Tarski proof variant in Lean, making the fixed point explicit?

**Answer**: Yes. The operator $T(S) = (\text{range}\ g)^c \cup g''(f''(S))$ on the complete lattice $\text{Set}\ \alpha$ is monotone. Its least fixed point $S^* = \text{lfp}(T)$ (via Mathlib's `OrderHom.lfp`) partitions $\alpha$ into two pieces:
- $a \in S^*$: use $f(a)$ (the forward injection)
- $a \notin S^*$: use $g^{-1}(a)$ (well-defined since $a \in \text{range}\ g$)

The resulting function $h : \alpha \to \beta$ is a bijection.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. **Define the operator**: $T(S) = (\text{range}\ g)^c \cup g''(f''(S))$ maps subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$. It is monotone because $\text{Set.image}$ preserves inclusion.

2. **Apply Knaster-Tarski**: By `OrderHom.lfp`, $T$ has a least fixed point $S^* = T(S^*)$ on the complete lattice $\text{Set}\ \alpha$.

3. **Extract properties**: From $S^* = (\text{range}\ g)^c \cup g''(f''(S^*))$:
   - $(\text{range}\ g)^c \subseteq S^*$ (base inclusion)
   - $S^{*c} \subseteq \text{range}\ g$ (contrapositive: $g^{-1}$ is defined outside $S^*$)
   - $g''(f''(S^*)) \subseteq S^*$ (closure under $g \circ f$)

4. **Build the bijection**: Injectivity: four cases by $S^*$-membership. Mixed cases give contradictions via the closure property. Surjectivity: for $b \in \beta$, either $b \in f''(S^*)$ or $g(b) \notin S^*$.
keyInsights: **One-Line Core**: The entire proof strategy is 'apply Knaster-Tarski to T(S) = (range g)ᶜ ∪ g''(f''S)'. Everything else is bookkeeping.
**No Orbits Needed**: Unlike the standard proof, there is no orbit classification (Type A/B/C). The lattice fixed point handles the partition automatically.
**Connection to Lattice Theory**: Schroeder-Bernstein is an instance of Knaster-Tarski on the power set lattice, connecting cardinal arithmetic to order theory.
**Fixed Point Is Explicit**: Unlike the classical Mathlib proof (which uses Classical.choice internally), the partition set S* is explicitly constructed as OrderHom.lfp and can be inspected.
**Three Proof Variants**: The gallery now has three CBS proofs: orbit decomposition (parent), Knaster-Tarski (this), and constructive finite (OQ-04), each using fundamentally different methods.
overview.text: A Knaster-Tarski proof of the Schroeder-Bernstein theorem in 207 lines, using Mathlib's OrderHom.lfp for the fixed point. The monotone operator T(S) = (range g)ᶜ ∪ g''(f''S) on Set α has a least fixed point S* that partitions α for the bijection. Fully verified: 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

sections.title: The Monotone Operator
sections.summary: Definition of the CBS operator T(S) = (range g)ᶜ ∪ g''(f''S) and proof of monotonicity.
sections.mathContext: Define $T : \mathcal{P}(\alpha) \to \mathcal{P}(\alpha)$ by $T(S) = (\text{range}\ g)^c \cup g''(f''(S))$. Since $S \subseteq S'$ implies $f''(S) \subseteq f''(S')$ implies $g''(f''(S)) \subseteq g''(f''(S'))$, the operator $T$ is monotone.

sections.title: The Knaster-Tarski Fixed Point
sections.summary: S* = lfp(T) via OrderHom.lfp. Proof that T(S*) = S*.
sections.mathContext: By the Knaster-Tarski theorem, every monotone endomorphism of a complete lattice has a least fixed point. Since $\mathcal{P}(\alpha) = \text{Set}\ \alpha$ is a complete lattice and $T$ is monotone, $S^* = \text{lfp}(T)$ exists and satisfies $T(S^*) = S^*$.

sections.title: Properties of S*
sections.summary: Key structural properties: complement of range ⊆ S*, closure under g∘f, and the contrapositive for surjectivity.
sections.mathContext: From $S^* = (\text{range}\ g)^c \cup g''(f''(S^*))$: (1) $(\text{range}\ g)^c \subseteq S^*$ trivially. (2) $a \notin S^* \Rightarrow a \in \text{range}\ g$ by contrapositive. (3) $g''(f''(S^*)) \subseteq S^*$ from the union. (4) If $g(b) \in S^*$ then $b \in f''(S^*)$ using injectivity of $g$.

sections.title: The Bijection
sections.summary: Piecewise bijection definition and basic specifications.
sections.mathContext: Define $h(a) = f(a)$ if $a \in S^*$, $h(a) = g^{-1}(a)$ if $a \notin S^*$. The function $g^{-1}$ is well-defined on $S^{*c}$ because $S^{*c} \subseteq \text{range}\ g$. Specification: $h(a) = f(a)$ for $a \in S^*$, and $g(h(a)) = a$ for $a \notin S^*$.

sections.title: Injectivity
sections.summary: Four-case proof that h is injective.
sections.mathContext: Four cases for $a_1, a_2$ with $h(a_1) = h(a_2)$: (1) Both in $S^*$: $f(a_1) = f(a_2) \Rightarrow a_1 = a_2$ by injectivity of $f$. (2,3) One in $S^*$, one not: $g(f(a_i)) = a_j$ but $g(f(a_i)) \in S^*$ by closure, contradicting $a_j \notin S^*$. (4) Both outside $S^*$: $g(h(a_1)) = g(h(a_2)) \Rightarrow a_1 = a_2$.

sections.title: Surjectivity
sections.summary: Two-case proof that h is surjective.
sections.mathContext: For $b \in \beta$: (1) If $b \in f''(S^*)$, then $b = f(a)$ for some $a \in S^*$, so $h(a) = b$. (2) If $b \notin f''(S^*)$, then $g(b) \notin S^*$ (since $g(b) \in S^* \Rightarrow b \in f''(S^*)$ by the preimage lemma). So $h(g(b)) = g^{-1}(g(b)) = b$.

sections.title: Main Theorems
sections.summary: Full Schroeder-Bernstein theorem recovered via the Knaster-Tarski construction.
sections.mathContext: Combining injectivity and surjectivity: given injections $f : \alpha \hookrightarrow \beta$ and $g : \beta \hookrightarrow \alpha$, there exists a bijection $\alpha \simeq \beta$, constructed explicitly via the Knaster-Tarski fixed point.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified Knaster-Tarski proof of the Schroeder-Bernstein theorem. The monotone operator T(S) = (range g)ᶜ ∪ g''(f''S) has its least fixed point computed via Mathlib's OrderHom.lfp, yielding the partition for the bijection.
conclusion.implications:
**Three Proof Methods Formalized**: The gallery now contains three fundamentally different CBS proofs: orbit decomposition (classical, via Mathlib), Knaster-Tarski (lattice-theoretic, this proof), and constructive finite (decidable, OQ-04). This demonstrates the theorem's deep connections across set theory, lattice theory, and constructive mathematics.

**Lattice Theory Connection**: By making the Knaster-Tarski structure explicit, this proof invites generalizations: any monotone operator on a complete lattice has fixed points, and many existence results in mathematics can be recast in this framework.
openQuestions: The Knaster-Tarski fixed point is the *least* fixed point of T. Is the greatest fixed point S** = gfp(T) equally useful? What is S** ∖ S* geometrically?
Can the Knaster-Tarski approach be extended to prove the Schroeder-Bernstein property in specific categories (e.g., well-ordered sets, divisible abelian groups)?
